investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion and Swarm Agent Quota Exceeded
investigation.summary: The remote-agent-create eval failed because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod due to exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm resources on the 2 eligible nodes, leaving the pod unscheduled for 141 seconds. Sibling checks remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime independently failed with HTTP 409 conflict errors indicating the swarm agent quota of 100 has been reached, meaning new agent creation attempts are being rejected at the API layer as well. All required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is absent because the agent never reached a running state.
investigation.rootCause: Two compounding infrastructure-layer failures are blocking remote agent creation in the production-api environment. First, the Kubernetes cluster has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector; the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector at all, and preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist. Second, the swarm layer is reporting that the org-scoped agent quota of 100 has been reached, causing POST /api/agents to return HTTP 409 for the sibling checks. The primary eval (remote-agent-create) failed at the VM scheduling layer before the quota error was even reached; the sibling checks hit the quota error directly. Neither failure is attributable to a code regression in the eval runner itself — the runner branch and expected-output contract are intact in source. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity/quota condition, not a confirmed user-traffic outage (no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence).

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: same HTTP 409 quota-exceeded response, corroborating the quota exhaustion signal across two independent sibling checks.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1854-1859: runner branch calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) — the probe logic is present and structurally correct; the failure is not a missing code path.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:254-258: expected-output contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the agent pod never started.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: the Kubernetes scheduler message explicitly states '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm', meaning all available VM slots on eligible nodes are consumed by existing pods. No preemption victims exist, so the pod cannot be scheduled until capacity is freed.

SECONDARY — Swarm agent quota reached at limit=100: the HTTP 409 responses on sibling checks indicate the swarm control plane is also rejecting new agent creation independently of the Kubernetes scheduling failure. This may reflect leaked or un-cleaned agents from prior eval runs accumulating against the quota.

TERTIARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: 4 nodes are structurally ineligible for this pod type, reducing the effective scheduling pool to 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are at VM capacity, there is zero scheduling headroom.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — Eval probe cleanup (withCleanup) may not be releasing VM resources or swarm agents from prior failed runs, causing quota and resource counts to grow over time. This is a hypothesis; no direct evidence of cleanup failure is present in the packet.

investigation.title: Remote Agent State Eval Failing: Swarm Agent Quota Exhausted (409 Conflict) Blocks createAgent, Preventing All Required Evidence Collection
investigation.summary: The remote-agent-state eval fails because POST /api/agents returns HTTP 409 with error code "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", meaning the swarm backend refuses to create a new remote agent for the eval probe. Because agent creation is the prerequisite step in the runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1879: createAgent), the probe never reaches the state-polling phase and therefore produces zero evidence, violating all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) defined in the expected-output contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 264.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend's per-org (or global) remote agent quota of 100 is at or above its limit at the time the eval runs. POST /api/agents returns 409 "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" before a new agent can be provisioned. The eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs:1879) fails immediately on this 409, so the probe exits with the conflict error rather than proceeding to poll agent state. No evidence object is written, causing the contract validator to flag all four required evidence fields as missing. This is an eval infrastructure failure reflecting a real infrastructure capacity or cleanup constraint on the production-api swarm backend; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — Swarm agent quota at capacity: The production-api swarm backend has reached its hard limit of 100 remote agents for the org or globally. Prior eval runs, leaked agents from failed cleanup, or real user agents may have consumed all available slots, causing every new POST /api/agents to return 409.

SECONDARY — Leaked eval agents from prior runs not cleaned up: The eval runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs:1877) to track and delete agents after each run. If cleanup failed in previous runs (e.g., due to the pod-scheduling failure seen in remote-agent-create), eval-created agents may have accumulated against the quota without being deleted.

TERTIARY — Kubernetes node resource exhaustion blocking new VM pods: The sibling remote-agent-create check reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on 2 of 6 nodes and node affinity mismatches on 4 nodes. This suggests the underlying VM pool for kata peer pods is also exhausted, which may be related to or compounding the quota issue.

LOWER — Transient quota enforcement race: The 409 could reflect a brief window where quota accounting is stale (e.g., agents being deleted but quota not yet decremented), though the identical failure across all three remote-agent checks in the same run makes a persistent quota exhaustion more likely than a transient race.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion and Swarm Agent Quota Exceeded
investigations.summary: The remote-agent-create eval failed because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod due to exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm resources on the 2 eligible nodes, leaving the pod unscheduled for 141 seconds. Sibling checks remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime independently failed with HTTP 409 conflict errors indicating the swarm agent quota of 100 has been reached, meaning new agent creation attempts are being rejected at the API layer as well. All required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is absent because the agent never reached a running state.
investigations.rootCause: Two compounding infrastructure-layer failures are blocking remote agent creation in the production-api environment. First, the Kubernetes cluster has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector; the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector at all, and preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist. Second, the swarm layer is reporting that the org-scoped agent quota of 100 has been reached, causing POST /api/agents to return HTTP 409 for the sibling checks. The primary eval (remote-agent-create) failed at the VM scheduling layer before the quota error was even reached; the sibling checks hit the quota error directly. Neither failure is attributable to a code regression in the eval runner itself — the runner branch and expected-output contract are intact in source. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity/quota condition, not a confirmed user-traffic outage (no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence).

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing, consistent with the probe aborting before createAgent could return.
sibling.remote-agent-state: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with 'conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', confirming the swarm quota is at or above its ceiling.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: same HTTP 409 quota-exceeded response, corroborating the quota exhaustion signal across two independent sibling checks.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1854-1859: runner branch calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) — the probe logic is present and structurally correct; the failure is not a missing code path.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:254-258: expected-output contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the agent pod never started.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: the Kubernetes scheduler message explicitly states '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm', meaning all available VM slots on eligible nodes are consumed by existing pods. No preemption victims exist, so the pod cannot be scheduled until capacity is freed.

SECONDARY — Swarm agent quota reached at limit=100: the HTTP 409 responses on sibling checks indicate the swarm control plane is also rejecting new agent creation independently of the Kubernetes scheduling failure. This may reflect leaked or un-cleaned agents from prior eval runs accumulating against the quota.

TERTIARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: 4 nodes are structurally ineligible for this pod type, reducing the effective scheduling pool to 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are at VM capacity, there is zero scheduling headroom.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — Eval probe cleanup (withCleanup) may not be releasing VM resources or swarm agents from prior failed runs, causing quota and resource counts to grow over time. This is a hypothesis; no direct evidence of cleanup failure is present in the packet.

investigations.title: Remote Agent State Eval Failing: Swarm Agent Quota Exhausted (409 Conflict) Blocks createAgent, Preventing All Required Evidence Collection
investigations.summary: The remote-agent-state eval fails because POST /api/agents returns HTTP 409 with error code "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", meaning the swarm backend refuses to create a new remote agent for the eval probe. Because agent creation is the prerequisite step in the runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1879: createAgent), the probe never reaches the state-polling phase and therefore produces zero evidence, violating all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) defined in the expected-output contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 264.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm backend's per-org (or global) remote agent quota of 100 is at or above its limit at the time the eval runs. POST /api/agents returns 409 "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" before a new agent can be provisioned. The eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs:1879) fails immediately on this 409, so the probe exits with the conflict error rather than proceeding to poll agent state. No evidence object is written, causing the contract validator to flag all four required evidence fields as missing. This is an eval infrastructure failure reflecting a real infrastructure capacity or cleanup constraint on the production-api swarm backend; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — Swarm agent quota at capacity: The production-api swarm backend has reached its hard limit of 100 remote agents for the org or globally. Prior eval runs, leaked agents from failed cleanup, or real user agents may have consumed all available slots, causing every new POST /api/agents to return 409.

SECONDARY — Leaked eval agents from prior runs not cleaned up: The eval runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs:1877) to track and delete agents after each run. If cleanup failed in previous runs (e.g., due to the pod-scheduling failure seen in remote-agent-create), eval-created agents may have accumulated against the quota without being deleted.

TERTIARY — Kubernetes node resource exhaustion blocking new VM pods: The sibling remote-agent-create check reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on 2 of 6 nodes and node affinity mismatches on 4 nodes. This suggests the underlying VM pool for kata peer pods is also exhausted, which may be related to or compounding the quota issue.

LOWER — Transient quota enforcement race: The 409 could reflect a brief window where quota accounting is stale (e.g., agents being deleted but quota not yet decremented), though the identical failure across all three remote-agent checks in the same run makes a persistent quota exhaustion more likely than a transient race.

The failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; this is an eval-level failure reflecting a real infrastructure capacity constraint.
